criteria.claim: runtime.todo.test.mjs asserts that a live idle-review payload really names an all-passed, unfinished plan (remaining [], next null, ready_to_finish true) in a scenario where such a plan exists, and the old loop executed zero times.

assertion_under_test.selector: const allPassed = reviews().filter(r => r.todo_unfinished?.some(p => p.attempt_id === plans.a.attempt_id));
assertion_under_test.gate: assert.ok(allPassed.length, 'no idle review named the all-passed plan before it was finished: ...')  (line 523)
assertion_under_test.per_payload: assert.deepEqual(payload.todo_unfinished.filter(p => p.attempt_id === plans.a.attempt_id), [{attempt_id: 'attempt-todo-a', node_key: 'execution.todo-full', next: null, remaining: [], ready_to_finish: true}])  (line 525)
assertion_under_test.fixture_order_gate: PROVIDER root branch, lines 276-277 + 287: the finish turn is only produced when an 'AItelier director review due:' message is already in options.messages

measured: Green on the unmodified tree (both baseline runs): the assert.ok(allPassed.length) at line 523 is what fails first in a regressed runtime (mutant 1 below), so its silence in the green run is evidence that at least one real idle-review payload named the all-passed plan a while it was unfinished.

A plan-a entry can only appear in todo_unfinished when awaitingFinish() was true for it (unfinishedWithoutChild, runtime.mjs:404-409), i.e. when its items had all passed AND no candidate report existed (finish_reported !== true, runtime.mjs:328-330). So each allPassed payload is a pre-finish witness by construction, and line 525 additionally pins next:null / remaining:[] / ready_to_finish:true.
Mutant 1 (mine, not the author's) reddens exactly this assertion with a real payload dump (see mutants[0]); restoring runtime.mjs byte-for-byte returns the file to green.

The old loop's vacuity was measured, not trusted: see vacuity_measurement. In the pre-fix scenario (test file from 16e51f3705, instrumented copy) zero idle reviews named plan a, so `for (const plan of review.todo_unfinished.filter(p => p.attempt_id === plans.a.attempt_id))` iterated over an empty array every time.
caveats: The witness is produced by the idle-review path (AITELIER_DSH_IDLE_REVIEW_MS=3000 in the fixture) after the root goes idle following the handback turn, so the scenario now depends on that timer. It is not flaky in what I measured (2 green runs) and it fails LOUD (line 523 / line 471 / the 75 s loop's rootDone assert) rather than hanging when the ordering breaks.

The loop is over all reviews that name plan a, so a post-finish review that still named plan a would pass line 525 (same shape). That case is caught elsewhere, not lost: the post-compaction snapshot deepEqual at lines 553-556 and runtime.finished-plan.test.mjs's 'the marker tracks the candidate report' both redden under mutant 3.

assert.* occurrences: runtime.todo.test.mjs 123 -> 124 (one net assertion ADDED); runtime.finished-plan.test.mjs 52 -> 52 (untouched by the diff).

The 11 deleted lines are: the old one-line comment about the all-pass plan, the old `for (const plan of review.todo_unfinished.filter(...))` loop and its deepEqual (7 lines), and 2 prose paragraphs in the doc. The loop's deepEqual is reproduced verbatim inside the new loop (lines 524-528) and is now guarded by assert.ok(allPassed.length) at 523 and applied to EVERY review naming plan a instead of only the last review naming plan b. Strictly stronger, not weaker: the old form could iterate zero times, and my vacuity_measurement shows it did.
The two assertions immediately above it are byte-identical: the plan-b deepEqual at 518-519 and the ready_to_finish symmetric check at 520-521.

The only other test-file change is a fixture precondition (PROVIDER lines 270-277, 287: finish now also requires a seen review message). It cannot mask a runtime defect: under mutant 1 the same scenario with the same gate reddens at line 523 with real payloads, and mutant 2/3 redden other assertions through the same gate. A gate can only delay the finish turn; the scenario has a 75 s wait whose failure path is assert.ok(rootDone) plus a 90 s test timeout, so a broken ordering fails loudly.

No assertion moved out from under a code path it used to cover: the big test still asserts the two handbacks (471), the plan-b review shape (518), everything in the snapshot (553-556) and the finish result (560-564), all of which I either saw redden under my mutants or saw green twice.
